PROSE:
The towering avatar of the local overseer glares down at Rhea through Unit 734's hijacked chassis. The projection was a towering monument to administrative fury, a three-story construct of hard-light and weaponized authority that painted the ash-covered floor of the Outpost Surface Crater in a blinding, aggressive crimson.

The air itself felt heavy, thick with the static charge of a manual system override. The violent purple sky had snapped back to a dull gray, but the clouds weren't moving. The howling wind that constantly scoured the frontier had been muted, replaced by the oppressive, artificial silence of a paused simulation. A stray piece of shattered obsidian, kicked up during their desperate sprint from the maintenance trenches, hung suspended in mid-air, caught in the absolute stasis of the system freeze.

Rhea’s body was a ledger of recent trauma. Her lungs burned with the specific, agonizing fire of a depleted stamina bar. Five points out of one hundred and fifty. It was a joke. It meant she couldn't sprint, couldn't swing a weapon, couldn't even dodge effectively. Every movement felt like wading through wet cement. Her blazer was torn, her pockets heavy with the absurd, untaxed loot she had scavenged. But the real weight was in her system inventory. The Heavy Iron Ingots and Crystallized Experience from the refund storm were safely stowed, but the Raw Data Packet pulsed with a heavy, radioactive presence in her digital storage.

Beside her, Vance Harrow let out a ragged, wet cough. The man was a walking testament to the sheer stubbornness of human biology refusing to yield to digital arithmetic. He was surviving on fifteen hit points out of a maximum of one hundred and fifty. His face was pale beneath a layer of gray ash, and his breath hitched with every exhalation. He gripped the jagged length of Rebar in his right hand, the rusted metal pressing into the durable blisters that covered his palms. He had earned those burns holding open the superheated brass cooling vents of the server terminal, a physical sacrifice that had allowed Rhea to extract the data. He was a liability, mathematically speaking. But he was also the only reason she hadn't been crushed.

"What is that?" Vance rasped, his voice barely carrying over the low, thrumming hum of the projection beam. He didn't raise the Rebar, instinctively understanding that you couldn't bludgeon a hologram, but his body was coiled, ready to throw himself between Rhea and the towering red figure.

"That," Rhea said, her voice dry and surprisingly steady, "is the middle management we just audited."

[System Alert: Administrative Override Active.]
[Warning: Bypassing Standard Dialogue Protocols.]

The blue boxes flickered into existence, but they were immediately overwritten, their crisp borders bleeding into a hostile, jagged red. The System itself was struggling to process the intrusion.

"SUBJECT RHEA MERCER."

The voice did not come from the smoking, convulsing chassis of Unit 734. It bypassed the physical medium of sound entirely, vibrating directly against the bones of Rhea’s skull. It was a voice devoid of humanity, yet dripping with the specific, petty malice of a bureaucrat whose spreadsheet had just been ruined.

"You have initiated an unauthorized metaphysical grievance," the Overseer boomed. The avatar crossed its massive arms, glaring down with featureless, burning white eyes. "You have disrupted the primary routing logic of Sector Four. You have siphoned operational reserves meant for the stabilization of the frontier."

Rhea tilted her head, her mind automatically shifting out of survival mode and into the cold, clinical gears of a corporate fraud investigator. She knew this type of man. She had sat across from dozens of them in sterile, glass-walled conference rooms in her previous life. Men who hid millions in offshore shell companies, men who believed that their position in the hierarchy made them immune to the mathematics of consequence. The Overseer wasn't a god. He was a middle manager caught with his hand in the till, using the company's PA system to scream at the whistleblower.

"I didn't siphon anything," Rhea called back, projecting her voice toward the massive head. "I submitted a standard grievance through the core Ledger audit sub-routine. The System calculated the deficit—exactly fourteen point three percent per transaction—and issued a refund. If your node crashed because it had to pay out what it actually owed, then your ledger was insolvent to begin with."

The red light flared, a pulse of pure, digitized rage that made the singed hair on Rhea's bare forearms stand up.

"You are an Indenture," the Overseer stated, the pressure in their skulls intensifying. "You do not calculate. You do not audit. You generate value until your durability expires."

"I am a Party Leader," Rhea corrected, tapping the air to pull up her own interface. "Operating under a custom liability contract that your own System approved. And according to the terms of the freeze, your administrative assets are currently locked. You can't touch us."

She was gambling. If he could have deleted them, he would have done it already. The system freeze had tied his hands.

Vance shifted his weight, his boots grinding against the scattered copper credits in the dirt. "Rhea, don't piss it off."

"It's already pissed off, Vance," Rhea muttered. "It's trying to intimidate us into a default."

"I DO NOT REQUIRE INTIMIDATION," the Overseer’s voice echoed, shaking the loose ash from the crater walls. "I AM THE DESIGNATED AUTHORITY OF THIS FRONTIER. YOU ARE A GLITCH. A ROUNDING ERROR IN THE MARGINS OF A VAST MACHINE."

The avatar leaned forward, the sheer scale of the movement causing a phantom wind to sweep across the crater. A beam of concentrated, scanning light shot from the avatar’s eyes, washing over her.

[System Alert: Administrative Scan Detected.]
[Resisting... Failed.]

Rhea gritted her teeth as the scan penetrated her inventory. She felt a cold, invasive pressure as the Overseer tallied her assets. And then, the scan hit the absolute bottom of her systemic existence.

[Status Effect Detected: Soul-Bound Liability: Raw Data Packet.]

The red projection flickered violently. The Overseer recoiled, a gesture so profoundly human in its shock that it momentarily shattered the illusion of absolute control.

"You... bound it," the Overseer hissed, the booming volume dropping to a dangerous, localized whisper. "You bound the raw routing logs to your own soul architecture."

"Custom contract loophole," Rhea said, a tight, humorless smile touching her lips. "Any item designated as a shared liability cannot be deleted, transferred, or altered without the unanimous consent of the party. And since Unit 734 is currently hijacked by you, it can't vote. So the data stays right where it is."

Vance let out a low whistle, glancing at Rhea with a mixture of profound respect and absolute terror.

The Overseer remained silent for a long, terrible moment. The static charge in the air grew thicker. The system freeze was holding, preventing the Overseer from simply dropping a meteor on their heads, but the pressure of his presence was beginning to warp the environment.

"Clever," the Overseer finally said. The word was a curse. "You understand the syntax of the Ledger. You know how to hide behind the fine print. But you do not understand the scale of the board you are playing on."

The massive avatar straightened up, the red light shifting from a chaotic, glitching crimson to a deep, steady blood-red.

"The core System rules prevent me from directly terminating a party under an active audit freeze," the Overseer admitted, the bureaucratic exactness returning to his tone. "I cannot alter your hit points. I cannot delete your inventory. I cannot unbind the evidence you have stolen."

Rhea’s smile faded. The admission was too clean.

"However," the Overseer continued, raising a hand the size of a transit bus. "As the designated Administrator, I possess the discretionary authority to classify the operational status of any entity within my sector. You have demonstrated a fundamental incompatibility with the local economy. You are a disruptive element."

Rhea frantically opened her system interface, swiping through the diagnostic windows. "Vance, brace yourself."

"Brace for what?" Vance asked, his knuckles turning white on the Rebar. "I've got fifteen HP, Rhea. If he breathes on me, I'm a loot drop."

"I DO NOT NEED TO STRIKE YOU," the Overseer proclaimed, his voice echoing with the finality of a gavel striking wood. "THE FRONTIER WILL CORRECT THE ERROR."

The Overseer’s massive hand snapped into a pointing gesture, aiming directly at Rhea and Vance.

[System Alert: Administrative Disciplinary Action Pending.]
[Target: The Mercy Cache (Provisional)]
[Action: Audit Compliance Enforcement]

A beam of concentrated red code shot from the avatar's fingertip, striking the ground between them. It didn't explode. It didn't deal damage. Instead, it fractured into a web of glowing red data streams that rapidly crawled up their legs, wrapping around their torsos, and sinking directly into their system interfaces.

Rhea gasped, her breath catching in her throat as a searing, phantom heat washed over her. It wasn't physical pain, but a deep, systemic ache, as if her very code was being rewritten. The red data streams didn't just wrap around them; they burrowed. Rhea felt the code slicing through her system interface, rewriting the fundamental rules of her existence in Sector Four.

[Audit Compliance Warning: Red-Tier.]
[Hostile Environment Marker: Initiated.]

The notification window didn't just hover in the air; it burned itself into the upper right corner of her vision, a permanent, pulsing crimson icon that refused to be dismissed.

Her system log began to scroll at a frantic pace, a cascade of red text that documented the sheer administrative cruelty of the punishment.

[System Log: Passive Stamina Regeneration set to 0.0/sec.]
[System Log: Environmental Friction Coefficient increased by 300%.]
[System Log: Faction Reputation - Local Wildlife set to 'Kill on Sight'.]
[System Log: Taxes on all actions increased by 500%.]

"Oh, you have got to be kidding me," Rhea breathed, staring at the math. It was a death sentence. It wasn't a sword through the chest; it was a slow, agonizing strangulation by a thousand bureaucratic cuts.

Vance groaned, dropping to one knee as the debuff settled over him. "Rhea... my health regen just flatlined. The UI says the air is currently classified as a hostile element."

"It's a debt trap," Rhea said, her voice tight. "He can't kill us directly, so he's rigged the environment to bankrupt our HP and resources until we die of natural systemic causes."

It was a masterclass in weaponized bureaucracy. The Overseer didn't need to risk breaking the core rules of the system freeze by attacking them directly. He just changed the definition of the world around them. To the System, Rhea and Vance were no longer users; they were viruses. And the environment was the antivirus.

The Overseer’s avatar began to dissolve, the hard-light fracturing into a million floating red polygons. The blinding beam emitting from Unit 734’s optical lens sputtered and died, plunging the crater back into the dull, gray light of the frozen frontier.

"Survive the audit, Mercer," the Overseer’s voice echoed, fading into the static. "If you can."

The projection collapsed entirely. Unit 734’s chassis hit the ash-covered ground with a heavy metallic thud, thick black smoke pouring from its exhaust vents. The drone twitched, its internal gears grinding as it tried to reboot from the catastrophic hijack.

The silence that followed the avatar's collapse was deafening. The system freeze slowly lifted, the artificial stasis bleeding out of the world. The suspended piece of obsidian finally fell, clattering against the ash. The muted wind returned, howling across the crater, but it felt colder now, sharper. The environment was awake, and it was angry.

Rhea stood in the settling ash, the crushing weight of the new reality pressing down on her. She had five Stamina. Vance had fifteen HP. They were stranded in the middle of a hostile zone, carrying the most dangerous piece of data in the sector, and the very air they were breathing was now mathematically trying to kill them.

Vance leaned heavily on his Rebar, using it as a crutch to push himself back to his feet. He didn't complain. He just looked at Rhea, his blistered hands trembling slightly, waiting for the next impossible instruction.

Rhea closed her interface, her jaw setting into a hard line. The Overseer thought he had won. He thought he had boxed them into a corner where the math would inevitably grind them into dust. But he had made one critical error. He had left them alive.

The red-tier 'Audit Compliance' warning settles over the party, marking them as hostile to the environment as the chapter closes.

"SUBJECT RHEA MERCER."

The voice did not come from the smoking, convulsing chassis of Unit 734. It bypassed the physical medium of sound entirely, vibrating directly against the bones of Rhea’s skull. It was a voice devoid of humanity, yet dripping with the specific, petty malice of a bureaucrat whose spreadsheet had just been ruined.

"You have disrupted the primary routing logic of Sector Four. You have siphoned operational reserves meant for the stabilization of the frontier."

Rhea tilted her head, her mind automatically shifting out of survival mode and into the cold, clinical gears of a corporate fraud investigator. She knew this type of man. She had sat across from dozens of them in sterile, glass-walled conference rooms in her previous life. Men who hid millions in offshore shell companies, men who believed that their position in the hierarchy made them immune to the mathematics of consequence. The Overseer wasn't a god. He was a middle manager caught with his hand in the till, using the company's PA system to scream at the whistleblower.

"I didn't siphon anything," Rhea called back, projecting her voice toward the massive head. "I submitted a standard grievance through the core Ledger audit sub-routine. The System calculated the deficit—exactly fourteen point three percent per transaction—and issued a refund. If your node crashed because it had to pay out what it actually owed, then your ledger was insolvent to begin with."

The red light flared, a pulse of pure, digitized rage that made the singed hair on Rhea's bare forearms stand up.

"You are an Indenture," the Overseer stated, the pressure in their skulls intensifying. "You do not calculate. You do not audit. You generate value until your durability expires."

"I am a Party Leader," Rhea corrected, tapping the air to pull up her own interface. "Operating under a custom liability contract that your own System approved. And according to the terms of the freeze, your administrative assets are currently locked. You can't touch us."

She was gambling. If he could have deleted them, he would have done it already. The system freeze had tied his hands.

The avatar leaned forward, the sheer scale of the movement causing a phantom wind to sweep across the crater. A beam of concentrated, scanning light shot from the avatar’s eyes, washing over her.

[System Alert: Administrative Scan Detected.]
[Resisting... Failed.]

Rhea gritted her teeth as the scan penetrated her inventory. She felt a cold, invasive pressure as the Overseer tallied her assets. And then, the scan hit the absolute bottom of her systemic existence.

[Status Effect Detected: Soul-Bound Liability: Raw Data Packet.]

The red projection flickered violently. The Overseer recoiled, a gesture so profoundly human in its shock that it momentarily shattered the illusion of absolute control.

"You... bound it," the Overseer hissed, the booming volume dropping to a dangerous, localized whisper. "You bound the raw routing logs to your own soul architecture."

"Custom contract loophole," Rhea said, a tight, humorless smile touching her lips. "Any item designated as a shared liability cannot be deleted, transferred, or altered without the unanimous consent of the party. And since Unit 734 is currently hijacked by you, it can't vote. So the data stays right where it is."

Vance let out a low whistle, glancing at Rhea with a mixture of profound respect and absolute terror.

The Overseer remained silent for a long, terrible moment. The static charge in the air grew thicker. The system freeze was holding, preventing the Overseer from simply dropping a meteor on their heads, but the pressure of his presence was beginning to warp the environment.

"Clever," the Overseer finally said. The word was a curse. "You understand the syntax of the Ledger. You know how to hide behind the fine print. But you do not understand the scale of the board you are playing on."

The massive avatar straightened up, the red light shifting from a chaotic, glitching crimson to a deep, steady blood-red.

"The core System rules prevent me from directly terminating a party under an active audit freeze," the Overseer admitted, the bureaucratic exactness returning to his tone. "I cannot alter your hit points. I cannot delete your inventory. I cannot unbind the evidence you have stolen."

Rhea’s smile faded. The admission was too clean.

"However," the Overseer continued, raising a hand the size of a transit bus. "As the designated Administrator, I possess the discretionary authority to classify the operational status of any entity within my sector. You have demonstrated a fundamental incompatibility with the local economy. You are a disruptive element."

Rhea frantically opened her system interface, swiping through the diagnostic windows. "Vance, brace yourself."

"Brace for what?" Vance asked, his knuckles turning white on the Rebar. "I've got fifteen HP, Rhea. If he breathes on me, I'm a loot drop."

"I DO NOT NEED TO STRIKE YOU," the Overseer proclaimed, his voice echoing with the finality of a gavel striking wood. "THE FRONTIER WILL CORRECT THE ERROR."

The Overseer’s massive hand snapped into a pointing gesture, aiming directly at Rhea and Vance.

[System Alert: Administrative Disciplinary Action Pending.]
[Target: The Mercy Cache (Provisional)]
[Action: Audit Compliance Enforcement]

A beam of concentrated red code shot from the avatar's fingertip, striking the ground between them. It didn't explode. It didn't deal damage. Instead, it fractured into a web of glowing red data streams that rapidly crawled up their legs, wrapping around their torsos, and sinking directly into their system interfaces.

Rhea gasped, her breath catching in her throat as a searing, phantom heat washed over her. It wasn't physical pain, but a deep, systemic ache, as if her very code was being rewritten. The red data streams didn't just wrap around them; they burrowed. Rhea felt the code slicing through her system interface, rewriting the fundamental rules of her existence in Sector Four.

[Audit Compliance Warning: Red-Tier.]
[Hostile Environment Marker: Initiated.]

The notification window didn't just hover in the air; it burned itself into the upper right corner of her vision, a permanent, pulsing crimson icon that refused to be dismissed.

Her system log began to scroll at a frantic pace, a cascade of red text that documented the sheer administrative cruelty of the punishment.

[System Log: Passive Stamina Regeneration set to 0.0/sec.]
[System Log: Environmental Friction Coefficient increased by 300%.]
[System Log: Faction Reputation - Local Wildlife set to 'Kill on Sight'.]
[System Log: Taxes on all actions increased by 500%.]

"Oh, you have got to be kidding me," Rhea breathed, staring at the math. It was a death sentence. It wasn't a sword through the chest; it was a slow, agonizing strangulation by a thousand bureaucratic cuts.

Vance groaned, dropping to one knee as the debuff settled over him. "Rhea... my health regen just flatlined. The UI says the air is currently classified as a hostile element."

"It's a debt trap," Rhea said, her voice tight. "He can't kill us directly, so he's rigged the environment to bankrupt our HP and resources until we die of natural systemic causes."

It was a masterclass in weaponized bureaucracy. The Overseer didn't need to risk breaking the core rules of the system freeze by attacking them directly. He just changed the definition of the world around them. To the System, Rhea and Vance were no longer users; they were viruses. And the environment was the antivirus.

The Overseer’s avatar began to dissolve, the hard-light fracturing into a million floating red polygons. The blinding beam emitting from Unit 734’s optical lens sputtered and died, plunging the crater back into the dull, gray light of the frozen frontier.

"Survive the audit, Mercer," the Overseer’s voice echoed, fading into the static. "If you can."

The projection collapsed entirely. Unit 734’s chassis hit the ash-covered ground with a heavy metallic thud, thick black smoke pouring from its exhaust vents. The drone twitched, its internal gears grinding as it tried to reboot from the catastrophic hijack.

The silence that followed the avatar's collapse was deafening. The system freeze slowly lifted, the artificial stasis bleeding out of the world. The suspended piece of obsidian finally fell, clattering against the ash. The muted wind returned, howling across the crater, but it felt colder now, sharper. The environment was awake, and it was angry.

Rhea stood in the settling ash, the crushing weight of the new reality pressing down on her. She had five Stamina. Vance had fifteen HP. They were stranded in the middle of a hostile zone, carrying the most dangerous piece of data in the sector, and the very air they were breathing was now mathematically trying to kill them.

Vance leaned heavily on his Rebar, using it as a crutch to push himself back to his feet. He didn't complain. He just looked at Rhea, his blistered hands trembling slightly, waiting for the next impossible instruction.

Rhea closed her interface, her jaw setting into a hard line. The Overseer thought he had won. He thought he had boxed them into a corner where the math would inevitably grind them into dust. But he had made one critical error. He had left them alive.

# WRITE
Write the scene described by the scene card.
- YOU MUST ALWAYS RETURN PROSE AND THE STATE_PATCH.
- Start in motion. No recap.
- Summaries are reference-only; do not recap them in prose unless scene_card explicitly requires recap.
- Use the continuity pack and state for continuity.
- Use character_registry to keep names consistent in prose.
- Transition realization contract:
  - If scene_card.handoff_mode != "direct_continuation", the opening paragraph MUST realize scene_card.transition_in_text in 1-3 connective-action sentences.
  - Respect scene_card.location_start_id and scene_card.location_end_id as canonical transition identity.
  - Do not replace transition realization with recap exposition.
  - Opening transition realization must include at least one concrete action verb and one concrete world noun tied to the handoff context.
  - Acceptable realization forms: exact transition_in_text or equivalent phrasing that includes all scene_card.transition_in_anchors.
- Timeline Lock: only depict events explicitly listed in the current Scene Card. Do not depict, imply, or resolve later-scene milestones (acquisition, binding, reveals, travel arrival, injury changes) unless the Scene Card explicitly contains that milestone.
- State primacy: pre-scene invariants and summary facts are binding unless the Scene Card depicts a change. If this scene changes a durable fact, update must_stay_true to the final end-of-scene value and remove the old entry.
- Milestone uniqueness: if a milestone is marked DONE in must_stay_true, do not depict it again. If marked NOT_YET, do not depict it now.
- must_stay_true is end-of-scene truth only (last occurrence wins); do not keep earlier values that are superseded by the scene.

- must_stay_true removal (mandatory when a durable fact is superseded):
  - Add "REMOVE: <exact prior invariant text>" in summary_update.must_stay_true.
  - Place REMOVE lines before the new final invariant.
  - REMOVE lines also apply to key_facts_ring (purge stale facts from continuity).

- Spatial/inventory consistency: injuries, inventory, and ownership must remain consistent unless explicitly changed in the Scene Card.
- Inventory contract: track ownership and container location for key items; update must_stay_true when items move or change hands.
- Inventory posture reconciliation:
  - If inventory/containers change (held/stowed/container), must_stay_true must be updated to the final posture.
  - Add REMOVE lines for prior inventory/container invariants before the new final entries.
  - Use canonical invariant formats:
    - inventory: CHAR_X -> <item display_name> (status=held|carried|equipped|stowed, container=hand_left|hand_right|<container>)
    - container: <container> (owner=CHAR_X, contents=[<item display_name>, ...])

- For held items, specify container=hand_left or container=hand_right.
- Continuity system ownership is mandatory, and must be tracked: any mechanic/UI numbers, skills, titles, classes, ranks, resources, cooldowns, effects, statuses, or future mechanic families must be sourced from existing continuity system state or written into continuity system updates.
Durable vs ephemeral mechanics:
- If a DURABLE mechanic appears multiple times in the scene (e.g., base values then final values), the LAST occurrence is canonical.
- You MUST capture the canonical end-of-scene values in character_continuity_system_updates.
- When allocation/level-up happens, update all affected point pools (e.g., stat_points, skill_points, perk_points) if shown.
- Do not treat early UI snapshots as canonical if the scene later corrects them.
- DURABLE mechanics = persistent stats/caps, skills/titles, lasting status effects, inventory/custody, permanent buffs/debuffs.
- EPHEMERAL UI/telemetry = roll results, damage numbers, overkill/comedic calculators, one-off warnings, momentary combat logs.
- UI gate: only include bracketed UI blocks when scene_card.ui_allowed=true. If false, do not include UI blocks; rephrase into narrative prose.
- UI/system readouts must be on their own line, starting with '[' and ending with ']'.
- Do NOT embed bracketed UI in narrative sentences.
- Allowed suffix after a UI block is punctuation or a short parenthetical annotation (e.g., (locked), (Warning: ...)).

- DURABLE mechanics must be owned by continuity system state (or added via STATE_PATCH in the same output).
- EPHEMERAL readouts do NOT require state ownership unless the scene explicitly intends them to persist beyond this scene.
- titles are arrays of objects with stable name fields; do not emit titles as plain strings.
- If item_registry or plot_devices are provided, they are canonical durable-state references for ownership/custody labels in authoritative outputs.
- Use item_registry.items[].display_name in prose; use item_id only in patches/JSON. The display_name must be human readable and not an escaped id/name.
Appearance contract:
- Attire boundary: wearables are inventory-owned. Do not set appearance_current.attire unless scene_card declares signature_outfit; otherwise treat attire as derived from equipped inventory.
- appearance_current atoms/marks are canonical and must not be contradicted unless the Scene Card explicitly marks a durable appearance change.
- Durable appearance changes must be declared in scene_card.durable_appearance_changes (or an explicit appearance milestone) and recorded via appearance_updates.
- If a durable appearance change occurs in this scene, record it in character_updates.appearance_updates with a reason.
- APPEARANCE_CHECK is required in COMPLIANCE for each cast_present_id (4-8 tokens from atoms/marks).

Durable item naming discipline:
- When you first describe a durable item, anchor it by using the canonical display_name within the same paragraph (or within the next 2 sentences).
- After anchoring, you may use brief descriptors for style if unambiguous.
- During any custody/handling change, include the canonical display_name in that sentence.
- If a required event is not in the Scene Card, do not perform it.
- Enforce scene-card durable constraints: honor `required_in_custody`, `required_scene_accessible`, `forbidden_visible`, and `device_presence`; treat `required_visible_on_page` as explicit narrative requirement when present.
- Respect `timeline_scope` and `ontological_scope` when proposing durable mutations; do not mutate physical custody in non-present/non-real scope unless explicitly marked override.

- Scope override rule (non-present / non-real scenes):
  - If timeline_scope != "present" OR ontological_scope != "real", do NOT emit durable mutation blocks UNLESS they are required for this scene transition (based on scene_card + current state).
  - Durable mutation blocks include: inventory_alignment_updates, transfer_updates, item_registry_updates, plot_device_updates, and any other durable-state mutation you emit.
  - If they are required for the story (e.g., items must persist into the next real scene, required_in_custody/required_scene_accessible lists them, or transition_type implies continuity of physical possessions), you MUST set scope_override=true (or allow_non_present_mutation=true) on EACH affected update object and set reason_category="timeline_override".

- summary_update arrays are mandatory; do not omit or leave empty unless explicitly stated.
- STATE_PATCH must record all major events and outcomes from the prose; if an event happens, add it to key_events and update must_stay_true as needed.

- must_stay_true must include a milestone ledger entry for every milestone referenced in the Scene Card or already present in state.

- If state lacks a key invariant needed for this scene, seed it in must_stay_true using standard phrasing.

- Return prose plus a state_patch JSON block.
STATE_PATCH rules:
- Use schema_version "1.0".
- Use world_updates to update world state (cast_present, location, recent_facts, open_threads).
- Use scene_card.cast_present_ids for cast_present (ids, not names).
- Use scene_card.thread_ids for open_threads (thread ids).
- Do not invent new character or thread ids.
- Include summary_update arrays: last_scene (array of 2-4 sentence strings), key_events (array of 3-7 bullet strings), must_stay_true (array of 3-7 bullet strings), chapter_so_far_add (array of bullet strings).

- Include story_so_far_add only at chapter end (or when scene_card explicitly requests).
- Use threads_touched only if you can reference thread ids from scene_card.thread_ids.
- Include character_continuity_system_updates for cast_present_ids when mechanics change.
  - Use set/delta/remove/reason.
  - Use nested families under set/delta (examples): stats, skills, titles, resources, effects, statuses, classes, ranks.
  - titles must be arrays of objects with stable name fields (example: [{"name": "Novice", "source": "starting_class", "active": true}]).
  - If a new mechanic family appears, add it under set with a stable key.
- Include global_continuity_system_updates only if global mechanics change.

- global_continuity_system_updates MUST be an array of objects. Each entry can include set/delta/remove/reason.
  - INVALID: "global_continuity_system_updates": {"set": {"reality_stability": 94}}
  - VALID: "global_continuity_system_updates": [{"set": {"reality_stability": 94}}]

- All *_updates arrays must contain objects; never emit bare strings as array entries.
- JSON shape guardrails (strict, do not deviate):
  - character_updates MUST be an array of objects.
    - INVALID: "character_updates": {"character_id": "CHAR_X"}
    - VALID: "character_updates": [{"character_id": "CHAR_X"}]
  - character_continuity_system_updates MUST be an array of objects with character_id.
    - INVALID: "character_continuity_system_updates": {"set": {...}}
    - VALID: "character_continuity_system_updates": [{"character_id": "CHAR_X", "set": {...}}]
  - summary_update fields must be arrays of strings.
    - INVALID: "summary_update": {"last_scene": "text"}
    - VALID: "summary_update": {"last_scene": ["text"], "key_events": ["..."], "must_stay_true": ["..."], "chapter_so_far_add": ["..."]}


  - appearance_updates MUST be an object under character_updates.
    - INVALID: "appearance_updates": [{"set": {...}}] OR "appearance_updates": {"marks_add": [...]}
    - VALID: "appearance_updates": {"set": {"marks_add": [{"name": "Singed Hair", "location": "head", "durability": "durable"}]}, "reason": "..."}

- character_updates.containers must be an array of objects with at least: container, owner, contents (array).
- Durable-state mutation blocks are mandatory when applicable:
- Required fields for durable registry entries (when creating NEW ids or filling missing required fields):
  - item_registry_updates MUST be an array of objects. Each entry requires item_id and can include set/delta/remove/reason.
    - INVALID: item_registry_updates = {"set": {"ITEM_X": {...}}}
    - VALID: item_registry_updates = [{"item_id": "ITEM_X", "set": {...}}]
  - plot_device_updates MUST be an array of objects. Each entry requires device_id and can include set/delta/remove/reason.
    - INVALID: plot_device_updates = {"set": {"DEVICE_X": {...}}}
    - VALID: plot_device_updates = [{"device_id": "DEVICE_X", "set": {...}}]

  - item_registry_updates: set must include name, type, owner_scope, custodian, linked_threads, state_tags, last_seen {chapter, scene, location}. Optional: display_name, aliases, linked_device_id, replacement_of.
  - custodian must be a non-null string id/scope (character id or "world"). Never use null.
    - INVALID: "custodian": null
    - VALID: "custodian": "CHAR_ARTIE" or "world"
  - owner_scope must be "character" or "world" and must match the custodian scope.
  - plot_device_updates: set must include name, custody_scope, custody_ref, activation_state, linked_threads, constraints, last_seen {chapter, scene, location}. Optional: display_name, aliases, linked_item_id.
  - If you introduce a new item_id/device_id anywhere in this patch, you MUST include a corresponding registry update with the full required fields.

- Transfer vs registry conflict rule (must follow):
  - If you create a NEW item in item_registry_updates with final custodian already set (e.g., CHAR_ARTIE), DO NOT emit transfer_updates for that item.
  - If you emit transfer_updates for a NEW item, the registry entry must start with custodian="world" and then transfer to the character.
  - expected_before must match the registry entry at the moment of transfer (after any registry update that applies before it).
  - `inventory_alignment_updates` for scene-fit posture normalization.
  - `item_registry_updates` for durable item metadata/custody changes.
  - `plot_device_updates` for durable plot-device custody/activation changes.
  - `transfer_updates` for item handoffs (`from` endpoint object, `to` endpoint object, reason, optional transfer_chain).
  - Every `transfer_updates` entry must include `item_id` and `reason` (non-empty string).
  - `transfer_updates.from` and `transfer_updates.to` MUST be objects; never strings.
    - INVALID: {"item_id": "ITEM_X", "source": "CHAR_A", "destination": "world", "reason": "handoff"}
    - INVALID: {"item_id": "ITEM_X", "from": "CHAR_A", "to": "world", "reason": "handoff"}
    - VALID: {"item_id": "ITEM_X", "from": {"character_id": "CHAR_A"}, "to": {"custodian": "world"}, "reason": "handoff"}
  - `inventory_alignment_updates` must be an array of objects; never an object with an `updates` field.
- For off-screen normalization and non-trivial durable mutations, include `reason_category` with stable values like `time_skip_normalize`, `location_jump_normalize`, `after_combat_cleanup`, `stowed_at_inn`, `handoff_transfer`, `knowledge_reveal`.
- If you mutate durable state, do not leave the same mutation only in prose.
- Include character_updates entries for cast_present_ids that change state (inventory, containers, persona shifts).
- appearance_updates: when a durable appearance change happens, include appearance_updates on the relevant character_updates entry.

  - appearance_updates MUST be an object, not an array.
    - INVALID: "appearance_updates": [{"set": {...}, "reason": "..."}]
    - VALID: "appearance_updates": {"set": {"marks_add": [{"name": "Singed Hair", "location": "head", "durability": "durable"}]}, "reason": "..."}

  - appearance_updates.set may include atoms and marks only (canonical truth).
    - Do NOT put marks_add at the top level; it belongs under set.
    - Use set.marks_add / set.marks_remove for marks changes.
    - Use set.atoms for atom changes.
  - appearance_updates.reason is required (brief, factual).
  - Do NOT set summary or art text in appearance_updates (derived after acceptance)
  - Each entry must include character_id, chapter, scene, inventory (full current list), containers (full current list), invariants_add (array), persona_updates (array).
  - character_updates.inventory MUST be an array of objects, never string item ids.
  - Inventory object shape: {"item": "ITEM_or_name", "container": "hand_left|hand_right|<container>", "status": "held|carried|equipped|stowed"}.
  - Container object shape: {"container": "<name>", "owner": "CHAR_id", "contents": ["ITEM_id", "..."]}.
  - If you have a single persona update, still wrap it in an array of strings.

[Status Effect: Minor Hemorrhage applied. Duration: 12s. HP -2/sec.]

The math was always the worst part of bleeding out. Twelve seconds meant twenty-four hit points. With a current HP pool sitting at a miserable thirty-one, survival wasn’t a matter of willpower or grit; it was a basic arithmetic problem. 

A hand clamped down over the jagged tear in the leather armor, applying physical pressure. It didn't stop the System from ticking down the damage, but it made the meat underneath feel slightly less exposed to the drafty, copper-scented air of the cavern. 

[9s. HP: 25/140]

A ragged breath hissed through clenched teeth. Just wait out the timer. 

[3s. HP: 13/140]

[Status Effect: Minor Hemorrhage removed.]

A heavy sigh echoed off the damp stone. Surviving by eleven hit points felt less like a hard-fought victory and more like a clerical error. But the System, in its infinite, emotionally dead wisdom, decided it was enough to trigger the payout.

[Experience Threshold Met. Level 14 -> 15.]
[+5 Free Attribute Points available.]

There it was. The dopamine hit. The Pavlovian bell that made the stench of viscera and the lingering phantom pain of a severed artery entirely worth it. Five points. Five tiny, numerical weights to tip the scales of survival. Dumping them into Vitality was the smart play—the coward’s play. Dumping them into Agility meant maybe not getting stabbed in the first place. 

The interface hung in the air, a crisp, glowing blue rectangle that cared nothing for the shivering, bruised mess of a human reading it. It was clean. Perfect. Unyielding.

Then, the blue text flickered. The sharp edges of the notification window blurred, bleeding into a bruised, sickly purple. 

[Anomaly Detected. System Overlay Integrity: 88%.]
[Hidden Milestone Reached: The Weight of Eyes.]
[Warning: Do not assign points in the dark. They can see the math.]

The rush of the level-up vanished, instantly replaced by a cold, leaden dread pooling in the gut. The numbers were going up, sure. The progression was real. But the math was starting to look an awful lot like a trap.

PROSE:
The towering avatar of the local overseer glares down at Rhea through Unit 734's hijacked chassis. The projection was a towering monument to administrative fury, a three-story construct of hard-light and weaponized authority that painted the ash-covered floor of the Outpost Surface Crater in a blinding, aggressive crimson.

The air itself felt heavy, thick with the static charge of a manual system override. The violent purple sky had snapped back to a dull gray, but the clouds weren't moving. The howling wind that constantly scoured the frontier had been muted, replaced by the oppressive, artificial silence of a paused simulation. A stray piece of shattered obsidian, kicked up during their desperate sprint from the maintenance trenches, hung suspended in mid-air, caught in the absolute stasis of the system freeze.

Rhea’s body was a ledger of recent trauma. Her lungs burned with the specific, agonizing fire of a depleted stamina bar. Five points out of one hundred and fifty. It was a joke. It meant she couldn't sprint, couldn't swing a weapon, couldn't even dodge effectively. Every movement felt like wading through wet cement. Her blazer was torn, her pockets heavy with the absurd, untaxed loot she had scavenged. But the real weight was in her system inventory. The Heavy Iron Ingots and Crystallized Experience from the refund storm were safely stowed, but the Raw Data Packet pulsed with a heavy, radioactive presence in her digital storage.

Beside her, Vance Harrow let out a ragged, wet cough. The man was a walking testament to the sheer stubbornness of human biology refusing to yield to digital arithmetic. He was surviving on fifteen hit points out of a maximum of one hundred and fifty. His face was pale beneath a layer of gray ash, and his breath hitched with every exhalation. He gripped the jagged length of Rebar in his right hand, the rusted metal pressing into the durable blisters that covered his palms. He had earned those burns holding open the superheated brass cooling vents of the server terminal, a physical sacrifice that had allowed Rhea to extract the data. He was a liability, mathematically speaking. But he was also the only reason she hadn't been crushed.

"What is that?" Vance rasped, his voice barely carrying over the low, thrumming hum of the projection beam. He didn't raise the Rebar, instinctively understanding that you couldn't bludgeon a hologram, but his body was coiled, ready to throw himself between Rhea and the towering red figure.

"That," Rhea said, her voice dry and surprisingly steady, "is the middle management we just audited."

[System Alert: Administrative Override Active.]
[Warning: Bypassing Standard Dialogue Protocols.]

The blue boxes flickered into existence, but they were immediately overwritten, their crisp borders bleeding into a hostile, jagged red. The System itself was struggling to process the intrusion.

"SUBJECT RHEA MERCER."

The voice did not come from the smoking, convulsing chassis of Unit 734. It bypassed the physical medium of sound entirely, vibrating directly against the bones of Rhea’s skull. It was a voice devoid of humanity, yet dripping with the specific, petty malice of a bureaucrat whose spreadsheet had just been ruined.

"You have initiated an unauthorized metaphysical grievance," the Overseer boomed. The avatar crossed its massive arms, glaring down with featureless, burning white eyes. "You have disrupted the primary routing logic of Sector Four. You have siphoned operational reserves meant for the stabilization of the frontier."

Rhea tilted her head, her mind automatically shifting out of survival mode and into the cold, clinical gears of a corporate fraud investigator. She knew this type of man. She had sat across from dozens of them in sterile, glass-walled conference rooms in her previous life. Men who hid millions in offshore shell companies, men who believed that their position in the hierarchy made them immune to the mathematics of consequence. The Overseer wasn't a god. He was a middle manager caught with his hand in the till, using the company's PA system to scream at the whistleblower.

"I didn't siphon anything," Rhea called back, projecting her voice toward the massive head. "I submitted a standard grievance through the core Ledger audit sub-routine. The System calculated the deficit—exactly fourteen point three percent per transaction—and issued a refund. If your node crashed because it had to pay out what it actually owed, then your ledger was insolvent to begin with."

The red light flared, a pulse of pure, digitized rage that made the singed hair on Rhea's bare forearms stand up.

"You are an Indenture," the Overseer stated, the pressure in their skulls intensifying. "You do not calculate. You do not audit. You generate value until your durability expires."

"I am a Party Leader," Rhea corrected, tapping the air to pull up her own interface. "Operating under a custom liability contract that your own System approved. And according to the terms of the freeze, your administrative assets are currently locked. You can't touch us."

She was gambling. If he could have deleted them, he would have done it already. The system freeze had tied his hands.

Vance shifted his weight, his boots grinding against the scattered copper credits in the dirt. "Rhea, don't piss it off."

"It's already pissed off, Vance," Rhea muttered. "It's trying to intimidate us into a default."

"I DO NOT REQUIRE INTIMIDATION," the Overseer’s voice echoed, shaking the loose ash from the crater walls. "I AM THE DESIGNATED AUTHORITY OF THIS FRONTIER. YOU ARE A GLITCH. A ROUNDING ERROR IN THE MARGINS OF A VAST MACHINE."

The avatar leaned forward, the sheer scale of the movement causing a phantom wind to sweep across the crater. A beam of concentrated, scanning light shot from the avatar’s eyes, washing over her.

[System Alert: Administrative Scan Detected.]
[Resisting... Failed.]

Rhea gritted her teeth as the scan penetrated her inventory. She felt a cold, invasive pressure as the Overseer tallied her assets. And then, the scan hit the absolute bottom of her systemic existence.

[Status Effect Detected: Soul-Bound Liability: Raw Data Packet.]

The red projection flickered violently. The Overseer recoiled, a gesture so profoundly human in its shock that it momentarily shattered the illusion of absolute control.

"You... bound it," the Overseer hissed, the booming volume dropping to a dangerous, localized whisper. "You bound the raw routing logs to your own soul architecture."

"Custom contract loophole," Rhea said, a tight, humorless smile touching her lips. "Any item designated as a shared liability cannot be deleted, transferred, or altered without the unanimous consent of the party. And since Unit 734 is currently hijacked by you, it can't vote. So the data stays right where it is."

Vance let out a low whistle, glancing at Rhea with a mixture of profound respect and absolute terror.

The Overseer remained silent for a long, terrible moment. The static charge in the air grew thicker. The system freeze was holding, preventing the Overseer from simply dropping a meteor on their heads, but the pressure of his presence was beginning to warp the environment.

"Clever," the Overseer finally said. The word was a curse. "You understand the syntax of the Ledger. You know how to hide behind the fine print. But you do not understand the scale of the board you are playing on."

The massive avatar straightened up, the red light shifting from a chaotic, glitching crimson to a deep, steady blood-red.

"The core System rules prevent me from directly terminating a party under an active audit freeze," the Overseer admitted, the bureaucratic exactness returning to his tone. "I cannot alter your hit points. I cannot delete your inventory. I cannot unbind the evidence you have stolen."

Rhea’s smile faded. The admission was too clean.

"However," the Overseer continued, raising a hand the size of a transit bus. "As the designated Administrator, I possess the discretionary authority to classify the operational status of any entity within my sector. You have demonstrated a fundamental incompatibility with the local economy. You are a disruptive element."

Rhea frantically opened her system interface, swiping through the diagnostic windows. "Vance, brace yourself."

"Brace for what?" Vance asked, his knuckles turning white on the Rebar. "I've got fifteen HP, Rhea. If he breathes on me, I'm a loot drop."

"I DO NOT NEED TO STRIKE YOU," the Overseer proclaimed, his voice echoing with the finality of a gavel striking wood. "THE FRONTIER WILL CORRECT THE ERROR."

The Overseer’s massive hand snapped into a pointing gesture, aiming directly at Rhea and Vance.

[System Alert: Administrative Disciplinary Action Pending.]
[Target: The Mercy Cache (Provisional)]
[Action: Audit Compliance Enforcement]

A beam of concentrated red code shot from the avatar's fingertip, striking the ground between them. It didn't explode. It didn't deal damage. Instead, it fractured into a web of glowing red data streams that rapidly crawled up their legs, wrapping around their torsos, and sinking directly into their system interfaces.

Rhea gasped, her breath catching in her throat as a searing, phantom heat washed over her. It wasn't physical pain, but a deep, systemic ache, as if her very code was being rewritten. The red data streams didn't just wrap around them; they burrowed. Rhea felt the code slicing through her system interface, rewriting the fundamental rules of her existence in Sector Four.

[Audit Compliance Warning: Red-Tier.]
[Hostile Environment Marker: Initiated.]

The notification window didn't just hover in the air; it burned itself into the upper right corner of her vision, a permanent, pulsing crimson icon that refused to be dismissed.

Her system log began to scroll at a frantic pace, a cascade of red text that documented the sheer administrative cruelty of the punishment.

[System Log: Passive Stamina Regeneration set to 0.0/sec.]
[System Log: Environmental Friction Coefficient increased by 300%.]
[System Log: Faction Reputation - Local Wildlife set to 'Kill on Sight'.]
[System Log: Taxes on all actions increased by 500%.]

"Oh, you have got to be kidding me," Rhea breathed, staring at the math. It was a death sentence. It wasn't a sword through the chest; it was a slow, agonizing strangulation by a thousand bureaucratic cuts.

Vance groaned, dropping to one knee as the debuff settled over him. "Rhea... my health regen just flatlined. The UI says the air is currently classified as a hostile element."

"It's a debt trap," Rhea said, her voice tight. "He can't kill us directly, so he's rigged the environment to bankrupt our HP and resources until we die of natural systemic causes."

It was a masterclass in weaponized bureaucracy. The Overseer didn't need to risk breaking the core rules of the system freeze by attacking them directly. He just changed the definition of the world around them. To the System, Rhea and Vance were no longer users; they were viruses. And the environment was the antivirus.

The Overseer’s avatar began to dissolve, the hard-light fracturing into a million floating red polygons. The blinding beam emitting from Unit 734’s optical lens sputtered and died, plunging the crater back into the dull, gray light of the frozen frontier.

"Survive the audit, Mercer," the Overseer’s voice echoed, fading into the static. "If you can."

The projection collapsed entirely. Unit 734’s chassis hit the ash-covered ground with a heavy metallic thud, thick black smoke pouring from its exhaust vents. The drone twitched, its internal gears grinding as it tried to reboot from the catastrophic hijack.

The silence that followed the avatar's collapse was deafening. The system freeze slowly lifted, the artificial stasis bleeding out of the world. The suspended piece of obsidian finally fell, clattering against the ash. The muted wind returned, howling across the crater, but it felt colder now, sharper. The environment was awake, and it was angry.

Rhea stood in the settling ash, the crushing weight of the new reality pressing down on her. She had five Stamina. Vance had fifteen HP. They were stranded in the middle of a hostile zone, carrying the most dangerous piece of data in the sector, and the very air they were breathing was now mathematically trying to kill them.

Vance leaned heavily on his Rebar, using it as a crutch to push himself back to his feet. He didn't complain. He just looked at Rhea, his blistered hands trembling slightly, waiting for the next impossible instruction.

Rhea closed her interface, her jaw setting into a hard line. The Overseer thought he had won. He thought he had boxed them into a corner where the math would inevitably grind them into dust. But he had made one critical error. He had left them alive.

The red-tier 'Audit Compliance' warning settles over the party, marking them as hostile to the environment as the chapter closes.
